questions: What guarantees is verify_post_anchor contractually required to retain from verify()?
Should GH #425, #430 and #443 be one phase or several?
Does pre-anchor tolerance for linkage breaks preserve the GH #55 consumer contract?
What test shape pins mode parity going forward?

findings.statement: verify_post_anchor honors 2 of doctrine section 14's contract elements fully, 1 partially, 1 not at all
No linkage pass in verify_post_anchor: _report_sequence has one call site repo-wide, inside verify() (473-595), not verify_post_anchor (615-725); spans AST-resolved
Forked fixture returns verify=1 with 2 BREAK lines and verify_post_anchor=0 clean; deterministic over 2 consecutive runs
The blind mode is consumed by substantiate Step 7.7 and by the skill-entry preflight

The Phase 258-262 working-tree fork is #443's class, not #425's; _duplicate_entry_numbers returns an empty list on the live ledger. No seal ran between break and repair, so there is no observed gate miss
Live ledger: 737 entries, 0 linkage breaks with and without tolerance, reconciled set empty. Adding the check costs this repository nothing

A re-anchored consumer ledger of the GH #55 shape carries 1 linkage break at the re-anchor seam, below the boundary. An unconditional _report_sequence call would fail every such consumer; the tolerance rule preserves them
boundary_entry = max(ok_entries) makes the reporting loop's error branch unreachable whenever the newest entry classifies ok; shared root of #425 and #430

test_post_anchor_verify.py has 11 tests and 0 covering linkage; test_post_anchor_tolerates_duplicate_number_strictly_before_boundary pins #425's behaviour as intended, so a fix must amend a green test
